title: Rajkumar Hirani Is Finally Doing OTT — and He's Bringing His Son and Circuit Along for the Ride
excerpt: After Munna Bhai, 3 Idiots, PK and Dunki, the man who makes India cry-laugh is making his streaming debut with 'Pritam and Pedro.' Arshad Warsi is back. So is a kid named Vir Hirani. July 3, JioHotstar.
body:
The trailer opens the way only a Hirani project can — not with a gun or a chase, but with a feeling. Two men who could not be more different, thrown into the same frame, the same case, the same gorgeous Goan light. One is old-school instinct in a rumpled uniform. The other is a hoodie-wearing tech whiz who treats a keyboard like a weapon. By the time the music kicks in, you already know you are going to root for both of them. That is the Hirani trick, and twenty-five years in, it still works.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=uCjkRVV0-qU</youtube>

**Rajkumar Hirani** — the director who turned *Munna Bhai M.B.B.S.*, *3 Idiots*, *PK* and *Dunki* into cultural events rather than mere releases — is finally making the leap to streaming. **Pritam and Pedro**, a Hotstar Special, drops July 3 on JioHotstar, and it carries the weight of being the first time Hirani has stepped outside the two-hour theatrical frame that made him India's most reliable hitmaker.

> "What excited me most about this story was the relationship at its heart. Pritam and Pedro come from completely different worlds and see life very differently, but they are forced into a journey together." — Rajkumar Hirani

That sentence could describe almost any film Hirani has ever made. The man has built an entire career on odd couples — the gangster and the medical college, the alien and the godmen, the dreamer and the system. Here the pairing is **Pedro** (Arshad Warsi), an instinct-driven cop exiled to the cyber cell as a punishment, and **Pritam** (newcomer **Vir Hirani**), a sharp young hacker who can see the digital world Pedro can barely switch on. A kidnapping pulls them together. Chaos, as the tagline promises, follows at every turn.

And here is where it gets personal. Vir Hirani is the director's son, and *Pritam and Pedro* is his launch. Letting your own child make his debut under your name is a high-wire act — every frame will be scrutinised for nepotism, every line dissected. But Hirani has never been a flashy launcher of star kids; he is a builder of *characters*. Early viewers of the trailer have been kind, noting that the young Hirani holds his own opposite seasoned scene-stealers. The bigger gamble is that Hirani is trusting his son to a series, not a film — twenty-odd hours of runway instead of two.

Then there is the reunion that has Munna Bhai loyalists in their feelings. **Arshad Warsi** and Hirani last shared real creative oxygen on *Lage Raho Munna Bhai* two decades ago, where Warsi's Circuit became one of Hindi cinema's most beloved sidekicks. Warsi is effortless in the trailer — that same loose, lived-in comic timing, now weathered into something warmer. "I think Raju has a little faith in me as an actor," he said at the launch, with the dry humility that has always made him impossible to dislike.


The ensemble is stacked the way Hirani's films always are, with faces you trust: **Vikrant Massey**, cast against type as a menacing antagonist; **Boman Irani**, the director's perennial good-luck charm; **Mona Singh**; Rajesh Sharma; Shruti Marathe. And at the launch, Warsi let slip that **Sanjay Dutt** — Munna Bhai himself — may turn up in a cameo, a detail that sent the fan forums into a frenzy.

The origin story is pure Hirani serendipity. He has said the idea arrived during the COVID lockdown, when the Mumbai Cyber Cell approached him to make a film about cybercrime — a subject most filmmakers would render as a grim procedural. Hirani, naturally, found the comedy and the humanity in it instead. **Avinash Arun**, the cinematographer-director behind some of the most painterly Indian frames of the decade, directs and shoots, which explains why a show about ATM scams and hacking looks this lush.

For the diaspora, the catch is the platform. *Pritam and Pedro* streams exclusively on **JioHotstar**, which means NRIs in the US, UK and Canada will need access through Hotstar's international tiers (or JioHotstar via VPN-adjacent workarounds that the comment sections are already swapping notes about). One overseas fan summed up the collective ache perfectly: "Would definitely like to watch Rajkumar's son's debut… but what can I do to get Jio Hotstar when not living in India?"

That frustration is, in its own way, the highest compliment. People do not beg for access to mediocre television. They beg for Hirani. July 3 cannot come soon enough.
